text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- "Terrorists" slaughter 31 civilians in the village of Sid el Kebir with swords and axes. They then dumped the bodies on the doorsteps of their victims' homes. Among the 31 victims were 11 women. Relatives could not identify some of the dead whose bodies were so badly disfigured.
- Doctors who examined the slaughtered villagers say the "terrorists" used saws to cut up the victims' bodies. About 50 villagers survived the killing by fleeing into nearby mountains.

- Prosecutor asks Algiers court to sentence El Watan editor Omar Belhouchet to four-month suspended jail term and 2,000 dinars ($360) fine over critical story about brother of a former prime minister.
- Italan businessmen involved in the Algerian market hail Italian state export agency SACE decision to resume credits and guarantees for exports to Algeria.

- The paper, which puts the number of those massacred in Sid el Kebir village at 32, says four more civilians were killed in the same night in Bouinan village, near Algiers. Among them was a pregnant woman.
